anf_compare.notes: No ANF or other public-domain English of this homily; translated from the Greek.

bible_refs.note: Φανερὰ ἔσται ἡ Γαλιλαία καὶ ὁ Κάρμηλος. Νῦν ἀναστήσομαι, λέγει κύριος, νῦν δοξασθήσομαι, νῦν ὑψωθήσομαι. Νῦν ὄψεσθε, νῦν αἰσχυνθήσεσθε follows LXX Isaiah 33:9b (φανερὰ ἔσται ἡ Γαλιλαία καὶ ὁ Κάρμηλος), 33:10 (νῦν ἀναστήσομαι, λέγει κύριος, νῦν δοξασθήσομαι, νῦν ὑψωθήσομαι) and 33:11a (νῦν ὄψεσθε, νῦν ...). The quotation opens in u01-rem-mid with 33:9a (ᾐσχύνθη ὁ Λίβανος, ἕλη ἐγένετο ὁ Σαρών), so the inline range starts at 33:9. Isaiah verse numbers are the same in LXX and Hebrew here; the English follows the wording Hesychius quotes.
«τὴν τοῦ δούλου μορφήν» is set off as a quotation in the source and echoes μορφὴν δούλου λαβών (Philippians 2:7).

choices.why: LXX 'will be manifest, exposed'; in the context of Lebanon put to shame and Sharon turned to marsh, 'laid bare' keeps the sense of exposure.

choices.term: τοῖς ἔθνεσιν τῶν παθῶν συστήσω τὴν ἀπάθειαν
choices.english: when I establish for the nations freedom from the passions
choices.why: ἀπάθεια with a genitive of what one is free from; the play παθῶν / ἀπάθειαν is noted in the translator notes, with the alternative 'through my sufferings'.
rejected: when I commend impassibility to the nations of the passions

choices.why: The human nature Christ took 'from you' (ἐξ ὑμῶν), the same as 'the form of the servant' in the next phrase.

choices.english: you who slander with words and are defeated by the facts
choices.why: The contrast is words against deeds; πράγματα are the events of the Resurrection that refute the slander.
rejected: slandering by sayings and being beaten by matters

choices.why: Standard doxology; ὅτι introduces the closing ascription.

lemmas.gloss: you will be put to shame

pass_a_gloss: [continuing Isaiah's words from u01-rem-mid] Manifest will be Galilee and Carmel. Now I will arise, says the Lord, now I will be glorified, now I will be exalted. Now you will see, now you will be put to shame. For toward the Jews he was stretching out the word: now I will arise when I raise Adam, whom the transgression threw down; now I will be glorified when to the nations I establish freedom from the passions; now I will be exalted, lifting up your firstfruits into the heavens and raising to the seat of the cherubim 'the form of the servant', which I have acquired from you; now you will see the types ceasing, the truth blossoming; now you will be put to shame, slandering with words and being defeated by deeds; because to God the glory, to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of the ages. Amen.
pass_b_english: '…Galilee and Carmel will be laid bare. Now I will arise,' says the Lord, 'now I will be glorified, now I will be lifted up. Now you will see, now you will be put to shame' (Isaiah 33:9–11).

For he was directing these words at the Jews: "Now I will arise, when I raise up Adam, whom the transgression cast down. Now I will be glorified, when I establish for the nations freedom from the passions. Now I will be lifted up, when I lift your firstfruits into the heavens and raise to the throne of the cherubim 'the form of the servant' (Philippians 2:7) that I have taken from you. Now you will see the types coming to an end and the truth in flower. Now you will be put to shame, you who slander with words and are defeated by the facts."
For glory belongs to God, to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
source_text:
Φανερὰ ἔσται ἡ Γαλιλαία καὶ ὁ Κάρμηλος. Νῦν ἀναστή σομαι, λέγει κύριος, νῦν
δοξασθήσομαι, νῦν ὑψωθήσομαι. Νῦν ὄψεσθε, νῦν αἰσχυνθήσεσθε.» Πρὸς γὰρ τοὺς
Ἰουδαίους τὸν λόγον ἀπετείνετο· νῦν ἀναστήσομαι ὅταν ἐγείρω τὸν Ἀδὰμ ὃν ἡ
παράβασις ἔρριψεν, νῦν δοξασθήσομαι ὅταν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν τῶν παθῶν συστήσω τὴν
ἀπάθειαν, νῦν ὑψω θήσομαι τὴν ὑμετέραν ἀπαρχὴν εἰς οὐρανοὺς ὑψῶν καὶ εἰς τὴν
καθέδραν τῶν χερουβὶν ἐπαίρων «τὴν τοῦ δούλου μορ φὴν» ἥνπερ ἐξ ὑμῶν
κέκτημαι, νῦν ὄψεσθε παυομέ νους τοὺς τύπους, ἀνθοῦσαν τὴν ἀλήθειαν, νῦν
αἰσχυνθή σεσθε συκοφαντοῦντες ῥήμασιν καὶ ἡττώμενοι πράγμασιν, ὅτι τῷ θεῷ ἡ
δόξα, τῷ Πατρὶ καὶ τῷ Υἱῷ καὶ τῷ ἁγίῳ Πνεύ ματι, νῦν καὶ ἀεὶ καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας
τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.

1
source_normalizations: Soft line-break splits joined (ἀναστή σομαι, ὑψω θήσομαι, μορ φήν, παυομέ νους, αἰσχυνθή σεσθε, Πνεύ ματι); no letters added.
Trailing page number '1' is an editorial page marker and is not translated.
reviewer: claude (Wave A review, clause by clause against the Greek)
review_notes: Row opens mid-quotation: Isaiah 33:9a ('Lebanon has been put to shame; Sharon has become marshland') closes u01-rem-mid, so the English opens with a leading ellipsis inside the quotation marks and the citation stands at the close of the quoted verses.

Every clause checked against the Greek: the four 'now' clauses of the verse, each expounded in the Lord's first-person voice (Adam raised, freedom from the passions for the nations, the firstfruits and the form of the servant lifted to the throne of the cherubim, types ceasing and truth in flower, slanderers defeated by the facts), then the Trinitarian doxology. No omission or addition.
Agency kept: 'whom the transgression cast down' (ἡ παράβασις subject of ἔρριψεν); 'that I have taken from you' (κέκτημαι, first person, ἐξ ὑμῶν).
Divine names capitalised: Lord (κύριος = God speaking in Isaiah), God, Father, Son, Holy Spirit.
Possible further echoes not cited inline because the wording is not close: 1 Corinthians 15:20 (ἀπαρχή) and Psalm 79:2 LXX / Psalm 80:1 (ὁ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τῶν χερουβίν).
